sentence: This project studies how a protein made only in the kidney can help protect kidney cells when the kidney is injured.
This project collects and supplies human and animal tissue samples and provides pathology services to cancer researchers.
This project tries to find out how changes in metabolism affect neural stem cells in the aging brain and whether their function can be restored.
This project tries to find out how genetic risk variants affect immune cells in the early stages of type 1 diabetes.
This project tests whether blocking an enzyme with a drug can prevent muscle wasting in chronic kidney disease.
This project uses colon organoids to find which genetic variants truly affect colorectal cancer risk and how their target genes act.
This project tries to find out how a small group of tumor cells escape treatment in colorectal cancer and how to reverse this.
This project studies how a signaling network involving a protein kinase drives the growth of glioblastoma.
This project studies what controls Wnt signaling in developing livers and how it sets up different zones of the liver.
This project studies RNA and DNA to find genetic causes of why patients with motor neuron diseases survive for very different lengths of time.
This project tries to find out how the hormone insulin controls the movement of bile acids in the liver.
This project uses genomic data to find genetic causes of severe childhood epilepsy and tests whether DNA methylation can show how a gene works.
This project builds mathematical and statistical methods to map gene regulatory networks from biomedical data and find possible causes of diseases.
This project builds Bayesian machine learning models and computer tools to study causes of cognitive decline and Alzheimer's Disease from long-term health data.
This project tests whether combining two drugs works better than pembrolizumab alone for muscle invasive bladder cancer.
This project studies how certain RNA molecules control the survival of retinal ganglion cells after optic nerve injury in mouse models.
This project uses mouse models to study how ribosome production shapes head and face development.
This project builds tools to manage, share and visualize large systems biology data on viruses and infectious disease.
This project studies when and where a sugar modification of proteins goes wrong in the brain, using Drosophila models of sleep and Alzheimer's disease.
